examples.name: Client onboarding
examples.description: Shows the current position in a five-step onboarding journey.

examples.name: Primary account setup
examples.description: Uses the brand appearance for a primary setup flow.

examples.name: Inverse
examples.description: Appears on a bold surface (color-background-neutral-bold-default). On the page's own surface the inverse selected dot almost disappears.

examples.name: Medium dots
examples.description: size="md" is a 12px dot in a 20px space; sm, the default, is an 8px dot in a 16px space.

examples.name: Custom value text
examples.jsx: <ProgressIndicator currentStep={2} totalSteps={4} label="Estate plan setup" getValueText={(step, total) => `Section ${step} of ${total}`} />

examples.name: Interactive dots
examples.description: Allows direct one-based step selection while remaining controlled from outside the component: each dot becomes a button named "Go to step N", and the root a named group. Update currentStep in onStepChange.
examples.jsx:
const [step, setStep] = useState(2);

<ProgressIndicator currentStep={step} totalSteps={5} label="Client onboarding" onStepChange={setStep} />

antiExamples.name: Unnamed indicator
antiExamples.reason: Without label (or aria-label / aria-labelledby), a screen reader hears only the step number. Name the journey: label="Client onboarding".

antiExamples.name: Progress Indicator for a task's progress
antiExamples.reason: Progress Indicator is position, not completion, and announces the upload as steps. Use Progress Bar for how much of a task is done: <ProgressBar value={30} label="Uploading documents" />.

antiExamples.name: Inverse on the page's own surface
antiExamples.reason: inverse is for a bold surface only; on the page's own surface its selected dot almost disappears. Use default or primary there.
